checks.source_statement: 如果数列收敛，那么它只有一个极限。
checks.source_quantifiers: For every epsilon>0, there exist n_1 and n_2 such that all n>n_1 satisfy |x_n-a|<epsilon/2 and all n>n_2 satisfy |x_n-b|<epsilon/2. Choose a natural n_0 strictly larger than both.
checks.independent_validation: The common index makes both tail bounds apply to the same term. Equality and non-strict triangle inequality are valid. The distance is fixed while epsilon is arbitrary; if d=|a-b|>0, taking epsilon=d contradicts d<epsilon. Hence a=b. The chosen index may depend on epsilon.

source_definitions: 数列有极限，而且只有一个，这样的数列叫做收敛数列
数列没有极限，这样的数列叫做发散数列
checks.independent_validation: Existence or absence of a finite limit gives the stated two cases, with uniqueness already proved. Divergence includes both unbounded sequences and bounded nonconvergent sequences; it does not mean only growth to infinity.

checks.source_contradiction: n<a+1 cannot hold for every n>n_1 because the natural numbers are unbounded.
checks.independent_validation: For any proposed finite limit a and its epsilon-1 threshold, choose a natural n>max(n_1,a+1). This contradicts the alleged tail upper bound. All displayed rearrangements preserve strict inequalities. Physical 83 contains the indispensable conclusion.

checks.source_conclusion: 在点 a 的邻域之外有数列的无穷多项，因此 a 不可能是极限。
checks.independent_validation: The two values 1 and -1 cannot both be in an open interval of length 1. Each occurs infinitely often by parity. For every threshold, a term remains outside the fixed radius-1/2 neighborhood, contradicting convergence. Infinitely many terms refers to indices, not distinct values.

checks.independent_epsilon_proof: For every epsilon>0 choose a natural N>=1/epsilon. Every natural n>N satisfies |x_n-2|=1/n<epsilon.
For every epsilon>0 choose a natural N>=1/epsilon. Every natural n>N satisfies |x_n-2|=|(-1)^n/n|=1/n<epsilon.

checks.independent_divergence_proof: For any proposed real a, the open interval (a-1/2,a+1/2) cannot contain both values 0 and 2. At least one parity, occurring infinitely often beyond every threshold, stays outside. Thus the sequence is bounded but has no finite limit.

checks.independent_growth_proof: For each real M choose a natural N>(M+1)/2. Every n>N has 2n-1>M.
checks.independent_finite_limit_contradiction: A finite limit a would require 2n-1<a+1 throughout an epsilon-1 tail, contradicted by sufficiently large natural indices.
checks.interpretation_note: Growth to positive infinity explains divergence but is not a finite source limit.
